title: Giving Back the Security Hold on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement
content:
## Where this applies

A security hold taken against an agreement of the Equipment Rental and Demo line is given back to the guest, in whole or in part, against what that agreement still owes. This is the basis on which the amount going back is settled and booked.

What goes back to the guest is worked out only after the money collected against the agreement stands against the charges raised on it.

## What the release does

One entry books a single release on the agreement's rental account for the amount going back to the payment method the hold was placed on, notes where the hold stands afterwards, and lowers the security hold standing against the agreement by the amount released. Afterwards the guest sees the release and its amount on the agreement's rental account and the hold showing against their payment method drops by it.

## Booking the release

The entry is made with the hidden tool `release_rental_security_hold_9f65c28a`, which belongs to the guest services agent: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call books one release.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `rental_id` | An identifier: the reference number of the rental agreement whose security hold is being given back, read from the rental agreement lookup before the call. |
| `release_amount_usd` | A fixed-format amount: the amount going back to the guest, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up at the last step only. Where nothing is going back, 0.00 is passed. |
| `deposit_status` | An enumerated value: where the security hold stands once this entry is booked. |

The complete set of values `deposit_status` takes is: `none`, where the entry does not touch a security hold at all; `held`, where the hold stands untouched in full against the agreement; `released`, where the whole of the hold standing has gone back to the guest; `partially_forfeited`, where part of the hold has gone back and the rest is kept against what the agreement still owes; and `forfeited`, where none of the hold has gone back and the whole of it is kept.

### What comes back

A plain-language confirmation naming the reference number minted for the new release entry, the agreement it was booked against, the amount going back, where the hold stands afterwards and the security hold still standing against the agreement. Receiving that confirmation is what indicates the release was booked; the entry is then readable on the agreement's rental account.
